images.title: Tanvi's walk in fifteenths
images.purpose: Show that thirds and fifths both become fifteenths, so 2/3 + 1/5 = 10/15 + 3/15 = 13/15 km.
images.composition: One short multiples row at the top, one long road strip for 1 km in the middle, and one sum line below, with wide space between them.
images.exact_structure: Top, centred: one row of three numbers 5, 10, 15 with 15 circled in reddish purple #CC79A7. Middle: one long road strip for 1 km cut by thin lines into 15 equal parts, with thicker lines after every 5 parts marking thirds. From the left: parts 1 to 10 filled teal #0072B2 for house to bus stop, parts 11 to 13 filled amber #E69F00 for bus stop to school, parts 14 and 15 plain. Centred below: one sum line. Exactly 1 multiples row, 1 strip, 15 equal parts, 10 teal, 3 amber, 2 plain.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: Find a common multiple of the denominators, rewrite, then add the numerators.
images.description: Multiples of 5 reach 15, which 3 also goes into; a 1 km strip in 15 equal parts shows 10 teal parts for 2/3 and 3 amber parts for 1/5, together 13/15 km.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at one thick third and count the 5 fifteenths inside it.

image_decisions.why: The multiples row and one strip in fifteenths show both steps of the method together.
